name: Terminal
style: Retro amber-phosphor CRT terminal: a zsh window where the headline prints as command output in glowing heavy mono with an inverse-video highlight, takeaways arrive as [ OK ]/[INFO]/[WARN] log lines and a block cursor waits at the prompt, all under scanlines, phosphor bloom, grain and vignette.
bestFor: Model releases, dev tools, open-source drops and API launches: news a developer would forward to their team chat.

principles.name: STEPPS: social currency and in-group identity
principles.how: Berger (Contagious, 2013) shows people share what makes them look in the know. The card speaks developer: a zsh prompt, a Homebrew-style ==> header, systemd-style [ OK ]/[WARN] tags, an 80×24 window title and a tmux-style status bar. Developers recognise their own tools and feel like insiders, so forwarding the card signals that they belong. Outsiders still get a plain-English headline.

principles.name: Novelty seeking
principles.how: Bunzeck & Düzel (2006) found that novel stimuli activate the brain's reward system. In a feed of photos and sans-serif slides, a glowing amber CRT screen with scanlines is an unexpected format, so it gets a second look before any word is read.

principles.name: Information-gap curiosity
principles.how: Loewenstein (1994) describes curiosity as the urge to close a specific gap in knowledge. The headline states a surprising, specific result (4 GB vs giants 20× its size). The last log line is a [WARN] that names an unresolved detail ('Benchmark #3 has devs arguing'), and the cursor blinks at an empty prompt. Both leave the reader wanting the next line, which the caption delivers.

principles.name: Isolation (Von Restorff) effect
principles.how: von Restorff (1933): the item that differs is noticed and remembered. Everything on the card is amber text on black except the highlight, which flips to inverse video (black on a glowing amber block). That one block is the focal point, and it still reads at thumbnail size.

hookFormula: A [small, specific spec] [open model / tool] just [beat / replaced] [bigger rival], [N× contrast]: e.g. "A 4 GB open model just beat giants 20× its size". Put the N× contrast in `highlight`, and make the last point a [WARN] that teases one unanswered detail.
captionTip: Open the caption by paying off the [WARN] line ("Benchmark #3: here's why devs are arguing ↓"). Put a one-line try-it command or link in the second line, then close with a question developers will answer in the comments ("Would you run this locally?").
notes: points render as log lines (max 4, per chunking). A point can start with [OK], [INFO], [WARN], [DONE], [FAIL], [ERR], [NEW] or [TIP] (or 'WARN: ...') to set its tag. Untagged points get [ OK ] for the first and [INFO] for the rest. If the headline can't fit at 64 px, the log clamps each line to 2 rows and then drops trailing lines, so the headline always wins. `source` sits on the right of the final prompt line (like zsh's RPROMPT); `handle` and `date` sit in the status bar. Design-specific fields: `command` (the typed command, default 'ai-news --latest') and `windowTitle` (default 'ai-news — zsh — 80×24'). Recolour with theme {"--fg": "#39FF7A", "--bg": "#010A04"} for green phosphor; every glow, rule and dim tone derives from --fg.
